 Follow Halloween is not a federal holiday. What that means
 Catherine Messier, USA TODAY NETWORK - New England Fri, October 23, 2026 at 9:08 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Halloween is fast approaching , falling this year on a Saturday, allowing many to observe the day without work or school.
 However, when Halloween is not on a weekend, the situation is not the same. While the holiday has been celebrated with tricks, treats and frights all across the country for centuries, Halloween is not recognized as an official holiday in the United States, on a federal or state level.
 Here's what they mean.
 Is Halloween a federal holiday?
 Will Nunnery of Kennedy Country Gardens on Rt. 3A in Scituate works on an early Halloween display at the greenhouse on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 No, Halloween is not a federal holiday. Although Halloween is widely celebrated across the country, it is not recognized as an official holiday on the federal or state level.
 Are businesses closed on Halloween?
 While post offices, banks, federal offices and certain businesses close on federal holidays, they remain open on Halloween.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Because Halloween 2026 falls on a Saturday, schools and businesses that are closed on weekends will remain closed on the holiday.

 What is a federal holiday?
 Federal holidays are holidays that are officially recognized by the United States government. All federal holidays are paid days off for federal employees, with closures observed at federal offices, financial institutions, schools and certain businesses.

 When are the federal holidays of 2026?
 The United States currently recognizes 11 holidays as federal holidays . Here are the holidays and their dates in 2026:
 Advertisement Advertisement New Year's Day – Thursday, Jan. 1
 Martin Luther King, Jr. Day – Monday, Jan. 19
 Washington's Birthday/Presidents Day – Monday, Feb. 16
 Memorial Day – Monday, May 25
 Juneteenth – Friday, June 19
 Independence Day – Saturday, July 4
 Labor Day – Monday, Sept. 7
 Columbus Day/Indigenous People's Day – Monday, Oct. 12
 Veterans Day – Wednesday, Nov. 11
 Thanksgiving Day – Thursday, Nov. 26
 Christmas Day – Friday, Dec. 25
